units.leftText: The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel: to know wisdom and instruction;
units.rightText: These are the proverbs of Solomon son of David, for gaining wisdom and discipline,

units.leftText: to receive instruction in wise dealing, to give prudence to the simple,
units.rightText: and for receiving instruction in wise living To impart prudence to the simple

units.leftText: that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; to understand a proverb and parables,
units.rightText: let the wise listen and gain instruction, by understanding the proverbs and parables,

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, My son, listen to your father’s instruction,
units.rightText: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, Listen, my son, to your father’s instruction,

units.leftText: for they will be a garland to grace your head, My son, if sinners entice you,
units.rightText: For they are a garland of grace on your head My son, if sinners entice you,

units.leftText: If they say, “Come with us. Let’s swallow them up alive like Sheol,
units.rightText: If they say, “Come along, let us lie in wait for blood, let us swallow them alive like Sheol,

units.leftText: We’ll find all valuable wealth. You shall cast your lot among us.
units.rightText: We will find all manner of precious goods; Throw in your lot with us;

units.leftText: my son, don’t walk on the path with them. for their feet run to evil.
units.rightText: my son, do not walk the road with them For their feet run to evil,

units.leftText: For the net is spread in vain in the sight of any bird; but these lay in wait for their own blood.
units.rightText: How futile it is to spread the net But they lie in wait for their own blood;

units.leftText: So are the ways of everyone who is greedy for gain. Wisdom calls aloud in the street.
units.rightText: Such is the fate of all who are greedy, Wisdom calls out in the street,

units.leftText: She calls at the head of noisy places. “How long, you simple ones, will you love simplicity?
units.rightText: in the main concourse she cries aloud, “How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways?

units.leftText: Turn at my reproof. Because I have called, and you have refused;
units.rightText: If you had repented at my rebuke, Because you refused my call,

units.leftText: but you have ignored all my counsel, I also will laugh at your disaster.
units.rightText: because you neglected all my counsel, in turn I will mock your calamity;

units.leftText: when calamity overtakes you like a storm, Then they will call on me, but I will not answer.
units.rightText: when your dread comes like a storm, Then they will call on me, but I will not answer;

units.leftText: because they hated knowledge, They wanted none of my counsel.
units.rightText: For they hated knowledge They accepted none of my counsel;

units.leftText: Therefore they will eat of the fruit of their own way, For the backsliding of the simple will kill them.
units.rightText: So they will eat the fruit of their own way, For the waywardness of the simple will slay them,

units.leftText: My son, if you will receive my words, so as to turn your ear to wisdom,
units.rightText: My son, if you accept my words if you incline your ear to wisdom

units.leftText: yes, if you call out for discernment, if you seek her as silver,
units.rightText: if you truly call out to insight if you seek it like silver

units.leftText: then you will understand the fear of the LORD, For the LORD gives wisdom.
units.rightText: then you will discern the fear of the LORD For the LORD gives wisdom;

units.leftText: He lays up sound wisdom for the upright. that he may guard the paths of justice,
units.rightText: He stores up sound wisdom for the upright; to guard the paths of justice

units.leftText: Then you will understand righteousness and justice, For wisdom will enter into your heart.
units.rightText: Then you will discern righteousness For wisdom will enter your heart,

units.leftText: Discretion will watch over you. to deliver you from the way of evil,
units.rightText: Discretion will watch over you, to deliver you from the way of evil,

units.leftText: who forsake the paths of uprightness, who rejoice to do evil,
units.rightText: from those who leave the straight paths from those who enjoy doing evil

units.leftText: who are crooked in their ways, to deliver you from the strange woman,
units.rightText: whose paths are crooked It will rescue you from the forbidden woman,

units.leftText: who forsakes the friend of her youth, for her house leads down to death,
units.rightText: who abandons the partner of her youth For her house sinks down to death,

units.leftText: None who go to her return again, Therefore walk in the way of good men,
units.rightText: None who go to her return So you will follow in the ways of the good,

units.leftText: For the upright will dwell in the land. But the wicked will be cut off from the land.
units.rightText: For the upright will inhabit the land, but the wicked will be cut off from the land,

units.leftText: My son, don’t forget my teaching, for they will add to you length of days,
units.rightText: My son, do not forget my teaching, for they will add length to your days,

units.leftText: Don’t let kindness and truth forsake you. So you will find favor,
units.rightText: Never let loving devotion or faithfulness leave you; Then you will find favor and high regard

units.leftText: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, In all your ways acknowledge him,
units.rightText: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, in all your ways acknowledge Him,

units.leftText: Don’t be wise in your own eyes. It will be health to your body,
units.rightText: Be not wise in your own eyes; This will bring healing to your body

units.leftText: Honor the LORD with your substance, so your barns will be filled with plenty,
units.rightText: Honor the LORD with your wealth then your barns will be filled with plenty,

units.leftText: My son, don’t despise the LORD’s discipline, for whom the LORD loves, he corrects,
units.rightText: My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD, for the LORD disciplines the one He loves,

units.leftText: Happy is the man who finds wisdom, For her good profit is better than getting silver,
units.rightText: Blessed is the man who finds wisdom, for she is more profitable than silver,

units.leftText: She is more precious than rubies. Length of days is in her right hand.
units.rightText: She is more precious than rubies; Long life is in her right hand;

units.leftText: Her ways are ways of pleasantness. She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her.
units.rightText: All her ways are pleasant, She is a tree of life to those who embrace her,

units.leftText: By wisdom the LORD founded the earth. By his knowledge, the depths were broken up,
units.rightText: The LORD founded the earth by wisdom By His knowledge the watery depths were broken open,

units.leftText: My son, let them not depart from your eyes. so they will be life to your soul,
units.rightText: My son, do not lose sight of this: They will be life to your soul

units.leftText: Then you shall walk in your way securely. When you lie down, you will not be afraid.
units.rightText: Then you will go on your way in safety, When you lie down, you will not be afraid;

units.leftText: Don’t be afraid of sudden fear, for the LORD will be your confidence,
units.rightText: Do not fear sudden danger for the LORD will be your confidence

units.leftText: Don’t withhold good from those to whom it is due, Don’t say to your neighbor, “Go, and come again;
units.rightText: Do not withhold good from the deserving Do not tell your neighbor,

units.leftText: Don’t devise evil against your neighbor, Don’t strive with a man without cause,
units.rightText: Do not devise evil against your neighbor, Do not accuse a man without cause,

units.leftText: Don’t envy the man of violence. For the perverse is an abomination to the LORD,
units.rightText: Do not envy a violent man for the LORD detests the perverse,

units.leftText: The LORD’s curse is in the house of the wicked, Surely he mocks the mockers,
units.rightText: The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, He mocks the mockers,

units.leftText: Listen, sons, to a father’s instruction. for I give you sound learning.
units.rightText: Listen, my sons, to a father’s instruction; For I give you sound teaching;

units.leftText: For I was a son to my father, He taught me, and said to me:
units.rightText: When I was a son to my father, he taught me and said,

units.leftText: Get wisdom. Don’t forsake her, and she will preserve you.
units.rightText: Get wisdom, get understanding; Do not forsake wisdom, and she will preserve you;

units.leftText: Wisdom is supreme. Esteem her, and she will exalt you.
units.rightText: Wisdom is supreme; so acquire wisdom. Prize her, and she will exalt you;

units.leftText: She will give to your head a garland of grace. Listen, my son, and receive my sayings.
units.rightText: She will set a garland of grace on your head; Listen, my son, and receive my words,

units.leftText: I have taught you in the way of wisdom. When you go, your steps will not be hampered.
units.rightText: I will guide you in the way of wisdom; When you walk, your steps will not be impeded;

units.leftText: Take firm hold of instruction. Don’t enter into the path of the wicked.
units.rightText: Hold on to instruction; do not let go. Do not set foot on the path of the wicked

units.leftText: Avoid it, and don’t pass by it. For they don’t sleep unless they do evil.
units.rightText: Avoid it; do not travel on it. For they cannot sleep

units.leftText: For they eat the bread of wickedness But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light
units.rightText: For they eat the bread of wickedness The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn,

units.leftText: The way of the wicked is like darkness. My son, attend to my words.
units.rightText: But the way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom; My son, pay attention to my words;

units.leftText: Let them not depart from your eyes. For they are life to those who find them,
units.rightText: Do not lose sight of them; For they are life to those who find them,

units.leftText: Keep your heart with all diligence, Put away from yourself a perverse mouth.
units.rightText: Guard your heart with all diligence, Put away deception from your mouth;

units.leftText: Let your eyes look straight ahead. Make the path of your feet level.
units.rightText: Let your eyes look forward; Make a level path for your feet,

units.leftText: My son, pay attention to my wisdom. that you may maintain discretion,
units.rightText: My son, pay attention to my wisdom; that you may maintain discretion

units.leftText: For the lips of an adulteress drip honey. but in the end she is as bitter as wormwood,
units.rightText: Though the lips of the forbidden woman drip honey in the end she is bitter as wormwood,

units.leftText: Her feet go down to death. She gives no thought to the way of life.
units.rightText: Her feet go down to death; She does not consider the path of life;

units.leftText: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me. Remove your way far from her.
units.rightText: So now, my sons, listen to me, Keep your path far from her;

units.leftText: lest you give your honor to others, lest strangers feast on your wealth,
units.rightText: lest you concede your vigor to others, lest strangers feast on your wealth,

units.leftText: You will groan at your latter end, and say, “How I have hated instruction,
units.rightText: At the end of your life you will groan and you will say, “How I hated discipline,

units.leftText: I haven’t obeyed the voice of my teachers, I have come to the brink of utter ruin,
units.rightText: I did not listen to the voice of my teachers I am on the brink of utter ruin

units.leftText: Drink water out of your own cistern, Should your springs overflow in the streets,
units.rightText: Drink water from your own cistern, Why should your springs flow in the streets,

units.leftText: Let them be for yourself alone, Let your spring be blessed.
units.rightText: Let them be yours alone, May your fountain be blessed,

units.leftText: A loving doe and a graceful deer— For why should you, my son, be captivated with an adulteress?
units.rightText: A loving doe, a graceful fawn— Why be captivated, my son, by an adulteress,

units.leftText: For the ways of man are before the LORD’s eyes. The evil deeds of the wicked ensnare him.
units.rightText: For a man’s ways are before the eyes of the LORD, The iniquities of a wicked man entrap him;

units.leftText: My son, if you have become collateral for your neighbor, you are trapped by the words of your mouth;
units.rightText: My son, if you have put up security for your neighbor, if you have been trapped by the words of your lips,

units.leftText: Do this now, my son, and deliver yourself, Give no sleep to your eyes,
units.rightText: then do this, my son, to free yourself, Allow no sleep to your eyes

units.leftText: Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, Go to the ant, you sluggard.
units.rightText: Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker;

units.leftText: which having no chief, overseer, or ruler, provides her bread in the summer,
units.rightText: Without a commander, it prepares its provisions in summer;

units.leftText: How long will you sleep, sluggard? A little sleep, a little slumber,
units.rightText: How long will you lie there, O slacker? A little sleep, a little slumber,

units.leftText: so your poverty will come as a robber, A worthless person, a man of iniquity,
units.rightText: and poverty will come upon you like a robber, A worthless person, a wicked man,

units.leftText: who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, in whose heart is perverseness,
units.rightText: winking his eyes, speaking with his feet, With deceit in his heart he devises evil;

units.leftText: Therefore his calamity will come suddenly. There are six things which the LORD hates;
units.rightText: Therefore calamity will come upon him suddenly; There are six things that the LORD hates, seven that are detestable to Him:

units.leftText: arrogant eyes, a lying tongue, a heart that devises wicked schemes,
units.rightText: haughty eyes, a heart that devises wicked schemes,

units.leftText: a false witness who utters lies, My son, keep your father’s commandment,
units.rightText: a false witness who gives false testimony, My son, keep your father’s commandment,

units.leftText: Bind them continually on your heart. When you walk, it will lead you.
units.rightText: Bind them always upon your heart; When you walk, they will guide you;

units.leftText: For the commandment is a lamp, to keep you from the immoral woman,
units.rightText: For this commandment is a lamp, this teaching is a light, to keep you from the evil woman,

units.leftText: Don’t lust after her beauty in your heart, For a prostitute reduces you to a piece of bread.
units.rightText: Do not lust in your heart for her beauty For the levy of the prostitute is poverty,

units.leftText: but if he is found, he shall restore seven times. He who commits adultery with a woman is void of understanding.
units.rightText: Yet if caught, he must pay sevenfold; He who commits adultery lacks judgment;

units.leftText: He will get wounds and dishonor. For jealousy arouses the fury of the husband.
units.rightText: Wounds and dishonor will befall him, For jealousy enrages a husband,

units.leftText: My son, keep my words. Keep my commandments and live!
units.rightText: My son, keep my words Keep my commandments and live;

units.leftText: Bind them on your fingers. Tell wisdom, “You are my sister.”

units.rightText: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, Come, let us take our fill of love till morning.

units.rightText: With her great persuasion she entices him; He follows her on impulse,

units.rightText: until an arrow pierces his liver, Now, my sons, listen to me,

units.rightText: Beside the gates to the city, “To you, O men, I call out,

units.leftText: You simple, understand prudence! Hear, for I will speak excellent things.
units.rightText: O simple ones, learn to be shrewd; Listen, for I speak of noble things,

units.leftText: For my mouth speaks truth. All the words of my mouth are in righteousness.
units.rightText: For my mouth will speak the truth, All the words of my mouth are righteous;

units.leftText: They are all plain to him who understands, Receive my instruction rather than silver,
units.rightText: They are all plain to the discerning, Receive my instruction instead of silver,

units.leftText: For wisdom is better than rubies. “I, wisdom, have made prudence my dwelling.
units.rightText: For wisdom is more precious than rubies, I, wisdom, dwell together with prudence,

units.rightText: To fear the LORD is to hate evil; Counsel and sound judgment are mine;

units.leftText: By me kings reign, By me princes rule,
units.rightText: By me kings reign, By me princes rule,

units.leftText: I love those who love me. With me are riches, honor,
units.rightText: I love those who love me, With me are riches and honor,

units.rightText: A man cannot be established through wickedness, A wife of noble character is her husband’s crown,

units.leftText: The thoughts of the righteous are just, The words of the wicked are about lying in wait for blood,
units.rightText: The plans of the righteous are just, The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood,

units.leftText: The wicked are overthrown, and are no more, A man shall be commended according to his wisdom,
units.rightText: The wicked are overthrown and perish, A man is praised according to his wisdom,

units.leftText: Better is he who is little known, and has a servant, A righteous man respects the life of his animal,
units.rightText: Better to be lightly esteemed yet have a servant, A righteous man regards the life of his animal,

units.leftText: He who tills his land shall have plenty of bread, The wicked desires the plunder of evil men,
units.rightText: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, The wicked desire the plunder of evil men,

units.leftText: An evil man is trapped by sinfulness of lips, A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth.
units.rightText: An evil man is trapped by his rebellious speech, By fruitful speech a man is filled with good things,

units.leftText: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, A fool shows his annoyance the same day,
units.rightText: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, A fool’s anger is known at once,

units.leftText: He who is truthful testifies honestly, There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword,
units.rightText: He who speaks the truth declares what is right, Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword,

units.leftText: Truth’s lips will be established forever, Deceit is in the heart of those who plot evil,
units.rightText: Truthful lips endure forever, Deceit is in the hearts of those who devise evil,

units.leftText: No mischief shall happen to the righteous, Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD,
units.rightText: No harm befalls the righteous, Lying lips are detestable to the LORD,

units.leftText: A prudent man keeps his knowledge, The hands of the diligent ones shall rule,
units.rightText: A shrewd man keeps his knowledge to himself, The hand of the diligent will rule,

units.leftText: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, A righteous person is cautious in friendship,
units.rightText: Anxiety weighs down the heart of a man, A righteous man is cautious in friendship,

units.leftText: The slothful man doesn’t roast his game, In the way of righteousness is life;
units.rightText: A lazy man does not roast his game, There is life in the path of righteousness,

units.leftText: A wise son listens to his father’s instruction, By the fruit of his lips, a man enjoys good things,
units.rightText: A wise son heeds his father’s discipline, From the fruit of his lips a man enjoys good things,

units.leftText: He who guards his mouth guards his soul. The soul of the sluggard desires, and has nothing,
units.rightText: He who guards his mouth protects his life, The slacker craves yet has nothing,

units.leftText: A righteous man hates lies, Righteousness guards the way of integrity,
units.rightText: The righteous hate falsehood, Righteousness guards the man of integrity,

units.leftText: There are some who pretend to be rich, yet have nothing. The ransom of a man’s life is his riches,
units.rightText: One pretends to be rich, but has nothing; Riches may ransom a man’s life,

units.leftText: The light of the righteous shines brightly, Pride only breeds quarrels,
units.rightText: The light of the righteous shines brightly, Arrogance leads only to strife,

units.leftText: Wealth gained dishonestly dwindles away, Hope deferred makes the heart sick,
units.rightText: Dishonest wealth will dwindle, Hope deferred makes the heart sick,

units.leftText: Whoever despises instruction will pay for it, The teaching of the wise is a spring of life,
units.rightText: He who despises instruction will pay the penalty, The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life,

units.leftText: Good understanding wins favor, Every prudent man acts from knowledge,
units.rightText: Good understanding wins favor, Every prudent man acts with knowledge,

units.leftText: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, Poverty and shame come to him who refuses discipline,
units.rightText: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline,

units.leftText: Longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, One who walks with wise men grows wise,
units.rightText: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, He who walks with the wise will become wise,

units.leftText: Misfortune pursues sinners, A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children,
units.rightText: Disaster pursues sinners, A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children,

units.leftText: An abundance of food is in poor people’s fields, One who spares the rod hates his son,
units.rightText: Abundant food is in the fallow ground of the poor, He who spares the rod hates his son,

units.leftText: Every wise woman builds her house, He who walks in his uprightness fears the LORD,
units.rightText: Every wise woman builds her house, He who walks in uprightness fears the LORD,

units.leftText: The fool’s talk brings a rod to his back, Where no oxen are, the crib is clean,
units.rightText: The proud speech of a fool brings a rod to his back, Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty,

units.leftText: A truthful witness will not lie, A scoffer seeks wisdom, and doesn’t find it,
units.rightText: An honest witness does not deceive, A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none,

units.leftText: Stay away from a foolish man, The wisdom of the prudent is to think about his way,
units.rightText: Stay away from a foolish man; The wisdom of the prudent is to discern his way,

units.leftText: Fools mock at making atonement for sins, The heart knows its own bitterness and joy;
units.rightText: Fools mock the making of amends, The heart knows its own bitterness,

units.leftText: The house of the wicked will be overthrown, There is a way which seems right to a man,
units.rightText: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, There is a way that seems right to a man,

units.leftText: Even in laughter the heart may be sorrowful, The unfaithful will be repaid for his own ways;
units.rightText: Even in laughter the heart may ache, The backslider in heart receives the fill of his own ways,

units.leftText: A simple man believes everything, A wise man fears and shuns evil,
units.rightText: The simple man believes every word, A wise man fears and turns from evil,

units.leftText: He who is quick to become angry will commit folly, The simple inherit folly,
units.rightText: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, The simple inherit folly,

units.leftText: The evil bow down before the good, The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbor,
units.rightText: The evil bow before the good, The poor man is hated even by his neighbor,

units.leftText: He who despises his neighbor sins, Don’t they go astray who plot evil?
units.rightText: He who despises his neighbor sins, Do not those who contrive evil go astray?

units.leftText: In all hard work there is profit, The crown of the wise is their riches,
units.rightText: There is profit in all labor, The crown of the wise is their wealth,

units.leftText: A truthful witness saves souls, In the fear of the LORD is a secure fortress,
units.rightText: A truthful witness saves lives, He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence,

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, In the multitude of people is the king’s glory,
units.rightText: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, A large population is a king’s splendor,

units.leftText: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, The life of the body is a heart at peace,
units.rightText: A patient man has great understanding, A tranquil heart is life to the body,

units.leftText: He who oppresses the poor shows contempt for his Maker, The wicked is brought down in his calamity,
units.rightText: Whoever oppresses the poor taunts their Maker, The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin,

units.leftText: Wisdom rests in the heart of one who has understanding, Righteousness exalts a nation,
units.rightText: Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning; Righteousness exalts a nation,

units.leftText: A gentle answer turns away wrath, The tongue of the wise commends knowledge,
units.rightText: A gentle answer turns away wrath, The tongue of the wise commends knowledge,

units.leftText: The LORD’s eyes are everywhere, A gentle tongue is a tree of life,
units.rightText: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, A soothing tongue is a tree of life,

units.leftText: A fool despises his father’s correction, In the house of the righteous is much treasure,
units.rightText: A fool rejects his father’s discipline, The house of the righteous has great treasure,

units.leftText: The lips of the wise spread knowledge; The sacrifice made by the wicked is an abomination to the LORD,
units.rightText: The lips of the wise spread knowledge, The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD,

units.leftText: The way of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, There is stern discipline for one who forsakes the way.
units.rightText: The LORD detests the way of the wicked, Discipline is harsh for him who leaves the path;

units.leftText: Sheol and Abaddon are before the LORD— A scoffer doesn’t love to be reproved;
units.rightText: Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD— A mocker does not love to be reproved,

units.leftText: A glad heart makes a cheerful face, The heart of one who has understanding seeks knowledge,
units.rightText: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, A discerning heart seeks knowledge,

units.leftText: All the days of the afflicted are wretched, Better is little, with the fear of the LORD,
units.rightText: All the days of the oppressed are bad, Better a little with the fear of the LORD

units.leftText: Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, A wrathful man stirs up contention,
units.rightText: Better a dish of vegetables where there is love A hot-tempered man stirs up strife,

units.leftText: The way of the sluggard is like a thorn patch, A wise son makes a father glad,
units.rightText: The way of the slacker is like a hedge of thorns, A wise son brings joy to his father,

units.leftText: Folly is joy to one who is void of wisdom, Where there is no counsel, plans fail;
units.rightText: Folly is joy to one who lacks judgment, Plans fail for lack of counsel,

units.leftText: Joy comes to a man with the reply of his mouth. The path of life leads upward for the wise,
units.rightText: A man takes joy in a fitting reply — The path of life leads upward for the wise,

units.leftText: The LORD will uproot the house of the proud, The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked,
units.rightText: The LORD tears down the house of the proud, The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked,

units.leftText: He who is greedy for gain troubles his own house, The heart of the righteous weighs answers,
units.rightText: He who is greedy for unjust gain brings trouble on his household, The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer,

units.leftText: The LORD is far from the wicked, The light of the eyes rejoices the heart.
units.rightText: The LORD is far from the wicked, The light of the eyes cheers the heart,

units.leftText: The ear that listens to reproof lives, He who refuses correction despises his own soul,
units.rightText: He who listens to life-giving reproof He who ignores discipline despises himself,

units.leftText: The plans of the heart belong to man, All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes,
units.rightText: The plans of the heart belong to man, All a man’s ways are pure in his own eyes,

units.leftText: Commit your deeds to the LORD, The LORD has made everything for its own end—
units.rightText: Commit your works to the LORD The LORD has made everything for His purpose—

units.leftText: Everyone who is proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD; By mercy and truth iniquity is atoned for.
units.rightText: Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for,

units.leftText: When a man’s ways please the LORD, Better is a little with righteousness,
units.rightText: When a man’s ways please the LORD, Better a little with righteousness

units.leftText: A man’s heart plans his course, Inspired judgments are on the lips of the king.
units.rightText: A man’s heart plans his course, A divine verdict is on the lips of a king;

units.leftText: Honest balances and scales are the LORD’s; It is an abomination for kings to do wrong,
units.rightText: Honest scales and balances are from the LORD; Wicked behavior is detestable for kings,

units.leftText: Righteous lips are the delight of kings. The king’s wrath is a messenger of death,
units.rightText: Righteous lips are a king’s delight, The wrath of a king is a messenger of death,

units.leftText: In the light of the king’s face is life. How much better it is to get wisdom than gold!
units.rightText: When a king’s face brightens, there is life; How much better to acquire wisdom than gold!

units.leftText: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil. Pride goes before destruction,
units.rightText: The highway of the upright leads away from evil; Pride goes before destruction,

units.leftText: It is better to be of a lowly spirit with the poor, He who heeds the Word finds prosperity.
units.rightText: It is better to be lowly in spirit among the humble Whoever heeds instruction will find success,

units.leftText: The wise in heart shall be called prudent. Understanding is a fountain of life to one who has it,
units.rightText: The wise in heart are called discerning, Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor,

units.leftText: The heart of the wise instructs his mouth, Pleasant words are a honeycomb,
units.rightText: The heart of the wise man instructs his mouth Pleasant words are a honeycomb,

units.leftText: There is a way which seems right to a man, The appetite of the laboring man labors for him,
units.rightText: There is a way that seems right to a man, A worker’s appetite works for him

units.leftText: A worthless man devises mischief. A perverse man stirs up strife.
units.rightText: A worthless man digs up evil, A perverse man spreads dissension,

units.leftText: A man of violence entices his neighbor, One who winks his eyes to plot perversities,
units.rightText: A violent man entices his neighbor He who winks his eye devises perversity;

units.leftText: Gray hair is a crown of glory. One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty;
units.rightText: Gray hair is a crown of glory; He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior,

units.leftText: Better is a dry morsel with quietness, A servant who deals wisely will rule over a son who causes shame,
units.rightText: Better a dry morsel in quietness A wise servant will rule over a disgraceful son

units.leftText: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, An evildoer heeds wicked lips.
units.rightText: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, A wicked man listens to evil lips;

units.leftText: Whoever mocks the poor reproaches his Maker. Children’s children are the crown of old men;
units.rightText: He who mocks the poor insults their Maker; Grandchildren are the crown of the aged,

units.leftText: Excellent speech isn’t fitting for a fool, A bribe is a precious stone in the eyes of him who gives it;
units.rightText: Eloquent words are unfit for a fool; A bribe is a charm to its giver;

units.leftText: He who covers an offense promotes love; A rebuke enters deeper into one who has understanding
units.rightText: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment

units.leftText: An evil man seeks only rebellion; Let a bear robbed of her cubs meet a man,
units.rightText: An evil man seeks only rebellion; It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs

units.leftText: Whoever rewards evil for good, The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam,
units.rightText: If anyone returns evil for good, To start a quarrel is to release a flood;

units.leftText: He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the righteous, Why is there money in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom,
units.rightText: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— Why should the fool have money in his hand

units.leftText: A friend loves at all times; A man void of understanding strikes hands,
units.rightText: A friend loves at all times, A man lacking judgment strikes hands in pledge

units.leftText: He who loves disobedience loves strife. One who has a perverse heart doesn’t find prosperity,
units.rightText: He who loves transgression loves strife; The one with a perverse heart finds no good,

units.leftText: He who becomes the father of a fool grieves. A cheerful heart makes good medicine,
units.rightText: A man fathers a fool to his own grief; A joyful heart is good medicine,

units.leftText: A wicked man receives a bribe in secret, Wisdom is before the face of one who has understanding,
units.rightText: A wicked man takes a covert bribe Wisdom is the focus of the discerning,

units.leftText: A foolish son brings grief to his father, Also to punish the righteous is not good,
units.rightText: A foolish son brings grief to his father It is surely not good to punish the innocent

units.leftText: He who spares his words has knowledge. Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise.
units.rightText: A man of knowledge restrains his words, Even a fool is considered wise if he keeps silent,

units.leftText: A man who isolates himself pursues selfishness, A fool has no delight in understanding,
units.rightText: He who isolates himself pursues selfish desires; A fool does not delight in understanding,

units.leftText: When wickedness comes, contempt also comes, The words of a man’s mouth are like deep waters.
units.rightText: With a wicked man comes contempt as well, The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters;

units.leftText: To be partial to the faces of the wicked is not good, A fool’s lips come into strife,
units.rightText: Showing partiality to the wicked is not good, A fool’s lips bring him strife,

units.leftText: A fool’s mouth is his destruction, The words of a gossip are like dainty morsels:
units.rightText: A fool’s mouth is his ruin, The words of a gossip are like choice morsels

units.leftText: One who is slack in his work The LORD’s name is a strong tower:
units.rightText: Whoever is slothful in his work The name of the LORD is a strong tower;

units.leftText: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city, Before destruction the heart of man is proud,
units.rightText: A rich man’s wealth is his fortified city; Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud,

units.leftText: He who answers before he hears, A man’s spirit will sustain him in sickness,
units.rightText: He who answers a matter before he hears it— The spirit of a man can endure his sickness,

units.leftText: The heart of the discerning gets knowledge. A man’s gift makes room for him,
units.rightText: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, A man’s gift opens doors for him,

units.leftText: He who pleads his cause first seems right— The lot settles disputes,
units.rightText: The first to state his case seems right Casting the lot ends quarrels

units.leftText: A brother offended is more difficult than a fortified city. A man’s stomach is filled with the fruit of his mouth.
units.rightText: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled;

units.leftText: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing,
units.rightText: Life and death are in the power of the tongue, He who finds a wife finds a good thing

units.leftText: The poor plead for mercy, A man of many companions may be ruined,
units.rightText: The poor man pleads for mercy, A man of many companions may come to ruin,

units.leftText: Better is the poor who walks in his integrity It isn’t good to have zeal without knowledge,
units.rightText: Better a poor man who walks with integrity Even zeal is no good without knowledge,

units.leftText: The foolishness of man subverts his way; Wealth adds many friends,
units.rightText: A man’s own folly subverts his way, Wealth attracts many friends,

units.leftText: A false witness shall not be unpunished. Many will entreat the favor of a ruler,
units.rightText: A false witness will not go unpunished, Many seek the favor of the prince,

units.leftText: All the relatives of the poor shun him; He who gets wisdom loves his own soul.
units.rightText: All the brothers of a poor man hate him — He who acquires wisdom loves himself;

units.leftText: A false witness shall not be unpunished. Delicate living is not appropriate for a fool,
units.rightText: A false witness will not go unpunished, Luxury is unseemly for a fool—

units.leftText: The discretion of a man makes him slow to anger. The king’s wrath is like the roaring of a lion,
units.rightText: A man’s insight gives him patience, A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion,

units.leftText: A foolish son is the calamity of his father. House and riches are an inheritance from fathers,
units.rightText: A foolish son is his father’s ruin, Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers,

units.leftText: Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep. He who keeps the commandment keeps his soul,
units.rightText: Laziness brings on deep sleep, He who keeps a commandment preserves his soul,

units.leftText: He who has pity on the poor lends to the LORD; Discipline your son, for there is hope;
units.rightText: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, Discipline your son, for in that there is hope;

units.leftText: A hot-tempered man must pay the penalty, Listen to counsel and receive instruction,
units.rightText: A man of great anger must pay the penalty; Listen to counsel and accept discipline,

units.leftText: There are many plans in a man’s heart, That which makes a man to be desired is his kindness.
units.rightText: Many plans are in a man’s heart, The desire of a man is loving devotion;

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD leads to life, then contentment; The sluggard buries his hand in the dish;
units.rightText: The fear of the LORD leads to life, The slacker buries his hand in the dish;

units.leftText: Flog a scoffer, and the simple will learn prudence; He who robs his father and drives away his mother
units.rightText: Strike a mocker, and the simple will beware; He who assaults his father or evicts his mother

units.leftText: If you stop listening to instruction, my son, A corrupt witness mocks justice,
units.rightText: If you cease to hear instruction, my son, A corrupt witness mocks justice,

units.leftText: Wine is a mocker and beer is a brawler. The terror of a king is like the roaring of a lion.
units.rightText: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler, The terror of a king is like the roar of a lion;

units.leftText: It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife, The sluggard will not plow by reason of the winter;
units.rightText: It is honorable for a man to resolve a dispute, The slacker does not plow in season;

units.leftText: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water, Many men claim to be men of unfailing love,
units.rightText: The intentions of a man’s heart are deep waters, Many a man proclaims his loving devotion,

units.leftText: A righteous man walks in integrity. A king who sits on the throne of judgment
units.rightText: The righteous man walks with integrity; A king who sits on a throne to judge

units.leftText: Who can say, “I have made my heart pure. Differing weights and differing measures,
units.rightText: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; Differing weights and unequal measures —

units.leftText: Even a child makes himself known by his doings, The hearing ear, and the seeing eye,
units.rightText: Even a young man is known by his actions— Ears that hear and eyes that see—

units.leftText: Don’t love sleep, lest you come to poverty. “It’s no good, it’s no good,” says the buyer;
units.rightText: Do not love sleep, or you will grow poor; “Worthless, worthless!” says the buyer,

units.leftText: There is gold and abundance of rubies, Take the garment of one who puts up collateral for a stranger;
units.rightText: There is an abundance of gold and rubies, Take the garment of the one who posts security for a stranger;

units.leftText: Fraudulent food is sweet to a man, Plans are established by advice;
units.rightText: Food gained by fraud is sweet to a man, Set plans by consultation,

units.leftText: He who goes about as a tale-bearer reveals secrets; Whoever curses his father or his mother,
units.rightText: He who reveals secrets is a constant gossip; Whoever curses his father or mother,

units.leftText: An inheritance quickly gained at the beginning Don’t say, “I will pay back evil.”
units.rightText: An inheritance gained quickly Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!”

units.leftText: The LORD detests differing weights, A man’s steps are from the LORD;
units.rightText: Unequal weights are detestable to the LORD, A man’s steps are from the LORD,

units.leftText: It is a snare to a man to make a rash dedication, A wise king winnows out the wicked,
units.rightText: It is a trap for a man to dedicate something rashly, A wise king separates out the wicked

units.leftText: The spirit of man is the LORD’s lamp, Love and faithfulness keep the king safe.
units.rightText: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD, Loving devotion and faithfulness preserve a king;

units.leftText: The glory of young men is their strength. Wounding blows cleanse away evil,
units.rightText: The glory of young men is their strength, Lashes and wounds scour evil,

units.leftText: The king’s heart is in the LORD’s hand like the watercourses. Every way of a man is right in his own eyes,
units.rightText: The king’s heart is a waterway in the hand of the LORD; All a man’s ways seem right to him,

units.leftText: To do righteousness and justice A high look and a proud heart,
units.rightText: To do righteousness and justice Haughty eyes and a proud heart—

units.leftText: The plans of the diligent surely lead to profit; Getting treasures by a lying tongue
units.rightText: The plans of the diligent bring plenty, Making a fortune by a lying tongue

units.leftText: The violence of the wicked will drive them away, The way of the guilty is devious,
units.rightText: The violence of the wicked will sweep them away The way of a guilty man is crooked,

units.leftText: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop The soul of the wicked desires evil;
units.rightText: Better to live on a corner of the roof The soul of the wicked man craves evil;

units.leftText: When the mocker is punished, the simple gains wisdom. The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked,
units.rightText: When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom; The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked

units.leftText: Whoever stops his ears at the cry of the poor, A gift in secret pacifies anger,
units.rightText: Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor, A gift in secret soothes anger,

units.leftText: It is joy to the righteous to do justice; The man who wanders out of the way of understanding
units.rightText: Justice executed is a joy to the righteous, The man who strays from the path of understanding

units.leftText: He who loves pleasure will be a poor man. The wicked is a ransom for the righteous,
units.rightText: He who loves pleasure will become poor; The wicked become a ransom for the righteous,

units.leftText: It is better to dwell in a desert land, There is precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise,
units.rightText: Better to live in the desert Precious treasures and oil are in the dwelling of the wise,

units.leftText: He who follows after righteousness and kindness A wise man scales the city of the mighty,
units.rightText: He who pursues righteousness and loving devotion A wise man scales the city of the mighty

units.leftText: Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue The proud and arrogant man—“Scoffer” is his name—
units.rightText: He who guards his mouth and tongue Mocker is the name of the proud and arrogant man —

units.leftText: The desire of the sluggard kills him, There are those who covet greedily all day long;
units.rightText: The craving of the slacker kills him All day long he covets more,

units.leftText: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination— A false witness will perish.
units.rightText: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable— A lying witness will perish,

units.leftText: A wicked man hardens his face; There is no wisdom nor understanding
units.rightText: A wicked man hardens his face, There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel

units.leftText: A good name is more desirable than great riches, The rich and the poor have this in common:
units.rightText: A good name is more desirable than great riches; The rich and the poor have this in common:

units.leftText: A prudent man sees danger and hides himself; The result of humility and the fear of the LORD
units.rightText: The prudent see danger and take cover, The rewards of humility and the fear of the LORD

units.leftText: Thorns and snares are in the path of the wicked; Train up a child in the way he should go,
units.rightText: Thorns and snares lie on the path of the perverse; Train up a child in the way he should go,

units.leftText: The rich rule over the poor. He who sows wickedness reaps trouble,
units.rightText: The rich rule over the poor, He who sows injustice will reap disaster,

units.leftText: He who has a generous eye will be blessed, Drive out the mocker, and strife will go out;
units.rightText: A generous man will be blessed, Drive out the mocker, and conflict will depart;

units.leftText: He who loves purity of heart and speaks gracefully The LORD’s eyes watch over knowledge,
units.rightText: He who loves a pure heart and gracious lips The LORD’s eyes keep watch over knowledge,

units.leftText: The sluggard says, “There is a lion outside! The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit.
units.rightText: The slacker says, “There is a lion outside! The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit;

units.leftText: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child; Whoever oppresses the poor for his own increase and whoever gives to the rich,
units.rightText: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich
